evidence: All three lesson objectives are addressed: types/properties/similarities/differences of plane shapes, parts of a circle, and perimeter of square, rectangle, trapezium, parallelogram, regular polygon, and circle.

The pack covers every specific shape named in the lesson objectives — square, rectangle, parallelogram, trapezium, regular hexagon, regular pentagon, and circle — including finding radius when circumference is given.
All nine circle parts named in the teacher's lesson (arc, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, segment, sector, tangent, and centre) are explained in the revision pack.
objective_curriculum_alignment.rationale: The revision pack maps directly and completely onto all three stated lesson objectives with no gaps. Every shape, formula, and circle part specified in the lesson plan is present and handled at the appropriate JSS1 level.

evidence: The pack follows the same three-part sequence the teacher planned: (1) types and properties of plane shapes, (2) parts of a circle, (3) perimeter calculations — matching the lesson's presentation order exactly.

The worked examples in the perimeter section reproduce the specific teacher evaluation questions almost verbatim (square 8 cm, rectangle 7×4 cm, pentagon 5 cm, parallelogram 6/5 cm, hexagon 5 cm, circumference 22 cm, breadth d), showing alignment with how the lesson was assessed.
The 'working backwards' subsection — finding radius from a given circumference and finding perimeter with an unknown algebraic side — mirrors the teacher's own examples and evaluation items 6 and 7.
taught_lesson_alignment.rationale: The revision pack replicates the teacher's lesson sequence, emphasis, and depth faithfully, including all the teacher's own evaluation questions as practice items with full worked solutions. It aligns well with what was taught and how it was assessed.

evidence: All perimeter formulas are mathematically correct: square (4s), rectangle 2(l+b), parallelogram 2(base+side), circumference 2πr or πd, and the worked numerical answers are all verified correct.
The octagon-diagonal question is correctly answered (6 triangles) with accurate reasoning using the formula n−2.

Circle-part definitions are accurate: tangent meets the radius at a right angle, diameter is a special chord through the centre, minor/major arc and segment distinctions are correct — no conceptual errors found.
scope_conceptual_correctness.rationale: Every formula, definition, and numerical answer checked out correctly; there are no out-of-scope topics introduced and no mathematical or conceptual errors anywhere in the pack.

evidence: Each section opens with plain-English explanations before introducing notation or formulas, making the material accessible to JSS1 students working alone at home (e.g., 'the total distance all the way around its outside edge').
Worked examples are laid out step-by-step with every line of working shown, and the 'Check your work' section gives full solutions so a student can self-correct without a teacher.
Practice questions in each section progress from recall/identification to calculation to algebraic generalisation, providing a useful graduated review for independent study.
clarity_usefulness.rationale: The pack is well-structured, uses age-appropriate language throughout, and provides sufficient scaffolding — including full answer keys — for a JSS1 learner to revise the lesson independently and check their own understanding.
